Summary of UTC-aware date utilities:

**`src/dates.js`** (new module)
- `isValidDate(dateString)`: Validates 'YYYY-MM-DD' format and checks for valid dates
  - Rejects invalid formats and impossible dates (Feb 30, etc.)
  - Uses UTC for all date validation
- `addDays(dateString, n)`: Adds n days to a date (n can be negative)
  - Returns new date in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format
  - Handles month/year boundaries correctly
  - All arithmetic in UTC
- `daysBetween(a, b)`: Calculates days between two dates (b minus a)
  - Returns whole days as integer (using Math.floor)
  - Handles month/year boundaries and leap years
  - All arithmetic in UTC

**`src/invoices.js`** (updated)
- Imported `isValidDate` from dates.js
- Removed internal `isValidDate()` function
- `createInvoice()` now uses centralized date validation

**`test/dates.test.js`** (new test file - 17 tests)
- Valid date acceptance and format validation
- Invalid format rejection
- Impossible date handling (Feb 30, non-leap Feb 29)
- Leap year logic (2000✓, 1900✗, 2024✓, 2023✗)
- `addDays()` with positive/negative/zero values
- Month and year boundary crossing
- `daysBetween()` positive and negative differences
- Large date range calculations
- Leap year edge cases
- Inverse relationship verification (addDays/daysBetween roundtrip)

**Test Results:** 111/111 passing ✓

All date operations use UTC exclusively; no local timezone dependencies anywhere in the date handling.
